props.heading: Software you can install in one line.
props.body: A headless CMS, the console that edits it, the renderer that publishes it and the tool that deploys the lot. Open source, MIT or MPL-2.0, already in other people's production.

props.heading: Install it
props.code:
dotnet add package BarakoCMS
docker compose up -d
barako open

props.label: barakoPress
props.code:
npm i barakopress
npx barakopress bindings-key baryo

props.label: BaryoVM
props.code:
dotnet tool install -g BaryoVM
baryovm up

props.title: Mapsicle
props.body: Object mapping, fourteen packages. Benchmarked on x64 and arm64 against AutoMapper and Mapperly, and the numbers say where it loses too.

props.title: barakoCMS
props.body: Event-sourced headless CMS on Marten and Postgres. 164 endpoints, 2,274 tests against real Postgres and MinIO. MPL-2.0, every module included.

props.title: Verdict
props.body: Result pattern, eight packages. The zero-allocation promise is enforced by benchmark: 0 B measured over 1.6M operations on 8 threads.

props.title: Carom
props.body: Retry, timeout, circuit breaker, bulkhead, rate limiting, fallback, hedging. 503 tests on .NET 8 and .NET 10. A leaner Polly.

props.title: Talaan
props.body: Spreadsheet and CSV reader, zero dependencies. barakoCMS consumes it as a published package, so the packaging is exercised for real.

props.title: Everything else
props.body: The two Umbraco packages and an early utility library, published under the same profile.

props.title: Hardening belongs in the deploy tool
props.body: What a cheap VM's auth log says, and the two commands we added because of it.

props.title: I started on an AS/400. Here is what AI-driven development actually changed
props.body: My first programming job was in 2012, writing RPG on an IBM midrange system. Fourteen years later I shipped a headless CMS with 126 endpoints.

props.question: Is any of it metered?
props.answer: No. No seat cap, no paid tier, no metered anything.

props.question: Can I run it myself?
props.answer: That is the only way it runs. Your VM, your database, your domain.

props.heading: Keep the workshop lit.
props.body: Everything here is open source and self-hostable. No paid tier, no seat cap, no metered anything. Sponsorship buys the CI minutes and the coffee.
